clearances_and_collisions.description: Finite collision-free geometry must preserve the 1.4 metre shared approach, the stone stoop landing, both forecourt beds, the rear cycle and refuse zones and the roof-bulkhead seat.

required_witness_views.description: Live frontage must show the raised stone stoop, panelled door and fanlight, symmetric sash-window grid, dressed-stone dressings, string course, cornice parapet, brick fields and forecourt planting.
Live working-face view must show the rear yard cycle and refuse relationship, opening depth and the brick-to-ground junction.
Live site view must show the clear central approach, both exact beds and planting, the rear cycle rack, entry planter and refuse location.
Live close view must show clear glazing, the brick reveal, the dressed-stone sill and flat-arch lintel, the timber sash frame and the room backing as one layered opening.
Live roofscape view must show the stone-capped cornice parapet, the seated screened bulkhead and a clean flat skyline.

base.description: A dressed-stone plinth course and the raised stone stoop landing resolve the brick-to-pavement junction and lift the formal floor above the street.

facade_rhythm.description: A strict symmetric grid of vertically proportioned openings, dressed-stone-framed and string-coursed, is centred on the panelled stone-surround door with its fanlight.

material_hierarchy.description: Red brick is primary, white dressed stone forms the plinth, lintels, sills, string course and door surround, panelled timber marks the door, glass reveals occupancy, the coped membrane caps the deck and metal stays accessory-scale.

middle.description: Red stock brick with white dressed-stone flat-arch lintels, sills and a continuous first-floor string course frames a symmetric grid of tall sash-proportioned openings.

plan.description: A twelve-point-eight by sixteen-point-five metre rectangular body runs the party-wall depth with a symmetric street facade and the stair core held to one flank.

section.description: A tall formal 3.0 metre ground floor sits beneath two upper storeys of diminishing window height and terminates at one coped stone-capped parapet.

structural_system.description: Solid loadbearing brick cross walls carry the party-wall line while concrete floor plates span between them beneath a flat parapet roof deck.

top_and_roofscape.description: A stone-capped cornice parapet closes the brick field above the top windows and screens one seated stair-and-tank bulkhead on the flat deck.

typology_and_context.description: A medium-density Georgian brick rowhouse forms one symmetric unit of a formal terrace, presenting a single ordered bay to a walkable street between shared party walls.

additional_features_and_extensions: Include dressed-stone dressings and string course, a stone-capped cornice, a screened roof bulkhead, two forecourt beds, a rear cycle rack, an entry planter and a rear refuse unit.
Exclude driveway, garage and future structural extension.
design_intent.serves_occupants_and_community: Households receive a formal daylit ground floor, a sheltered shared address and separated servicing while the street receives a dignified symmetric brick-and-stone terrace bay with planting.
special_needs_and_features: Keep the 1.4 metre central stoop approach on the symmetry axis unobstructed.
Give every occupied storey egress-scale tall windows.
Hold cycle storage and refuse in the rear yard off the formal front forecourt.
design_intent.style_and_architecture: Red-brick Georgian terrace with white dressed-stone plinth, flat-arch lintels, sills, a first-floor string course, a symmetric sash-proportioned window grid, a stone-capped cornice parapet and a panelled stone-surround door with a fanlight.

additional_features_and_extensions.decision: Author the dressed-stone stoop, panelled fanlit door, complete sash openings with stone lintels and sills, the string course, a stone-capped cornice, a screened roof bulkhead, two forecourt planting beds with exact plants, a rear cycle rack, an entry planter and a rear refuse unit while omitting a driveway and future extension envelope.
additional_features_and_extensions.reason: These exact parts make the period parcel maintained and inhabited, while excluding vehicle circulation protects the formal pedestrian stoop and the symmetric forecourt of a party-wall unit.
